newsitem.title: UK: Brady debt mostly unchanged in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Brady debt mostly unchanged in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Brady bond prices were basically unchanged in dull activity on Thursday and traders said prices were likely to remain rangebound ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting next week. "The FOMC clearly is keeping the market on its toes. I don't think the market is expecting a (U.S. interest) rate hike but nonetheless it dries up a little bit ahead of these types of events," said a Brady bond trader at a European bank.
The emerging debt market will also look to the U.S. Treasury market and stock market ahead for direction, dealers said.
Other data the market will focus on is U.S. gross domestic product (GDP) due out on Friday.
"I guess people are looking at the U.S. bond market which is what they tend to do when there is no news," another trader at a European bank said.
Among Eastern European debt instruments, Russian Vneshekonombank dollar loans were 1/8 firmer at 91-5/8 bid and Bulgarian IABs were 3/8 stronger at 71-1/8 bid.
Poland's Brady bonds were unchanged ahead of its Yankee bond issue expected to be priced today.
The expected $300 million bond issue is set to be divided into two tranches with maturities of seven years and possibly 20 years.
In the Latin Brady market, prices were uchanged to slightly firmer in thin trade.
Argentine FRBs were 1/8 firmer at 93-7/8 bid, Brazilian "C" bonds were 1/8 better at 80-3/4 bid and Venezeulan disount bonds were uncahnged at 88-3/4 bid.
